title: Every bridge fixes the last one's weakness

beats.text: You've built a bridge: a few planks over the stream.
Then a wagon of stone rolls on. The top squeezes, the bottom stretches, and wood tears. Snap.
So you build an arch. Its stones only squeeze each other, and stone loves that. The wagon rolls right across.
Then the railway must cross the wide river, where tall ships sail. Arches here put piers in their path.
So you use triangles. Push a square and it folds; a triangle can't. One light steel span carries the train.
Then the city must cross a whole bay. A truss that long sags under its own weight.
So you hang the road from two towers and two huge cables. Steel wire loves being pulled.
But summer comes. Hot steel grows, and the trapped deck buckles.
So you add steel fingers that let the deck slide in and out.
Then the wind twists the thin deck, like Tacoma Narrows in 1940.
So you brace it with a deep truss, and the wind slides past.
Today the longest span is over two kilometres. Which bridge would you trust in a storm?

cta: Which bridge would you trust in a storm?
